verses.text: Then the man brought me to the gate facing east.
I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing waters, and the land shone with his glory.
What I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and like the visions I had seen by the Kebar River. I fell face down on the ground.
The glory of the LORD came into the temple through the gate facing east.
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard, and I saw the glory of the LORD filling the temple.
While the man stood beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple.

He said, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place where I rest my feet. I will live here among the people of Israel forever. The people of Israel and their kings will never again dishonor my holy name by their unfaithfulness and by the dead bodies of their kings at their high places.

They built their doorways right next to my doorways and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them. They dishonored my holy name with the disgusting things they did, so I destroyed them in my anger.
Now let them put away their unfaithfulness and the dead bodies of their kings far from me. Then I will live among them forever.
"Son of man, describe the temple to the people of Israel, so they will be ashamed of their sins. Let them study its plan.

If they are ashamed of everything they have done, show them the design of the temple: its layout, its exits and entrances, its whole design, and all its rules and laws. Write these down while they watch, so they can keep its whole design and follow all its rules.
"This is the law of the temple: the whole area around it on top of the mountain will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the temple.

"These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits, each being a cubit and a handbreadth. Its gutter is one cubit deep and one cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge. This is the base of the altar.
From the gutter on the ground up to the lower ledge is two cubits, and the ledge is one cubit wide. From the smaller ledge up to the larger ledge is four cubits, and that ledge is one cubit wide.
The altar hearth is four cubits high, and four horns stick up from the hearth.
The altar hearth is square, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
The upper ledge is also square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide. It has a rim of half a cubit and a gutter of one cubit all around. The steps of the altar face east."
Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the rules for the altar when it is built, so that burnt offerings can be offered on it and blood can be sprinkled on it.
Give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests from the family of Zadok, who come near to serve me, says the Lord GOD.
Take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the upper ledge, and on the rim all around. This is how you will purify the altar and make it right for use.
Then take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the proper place in the temple area, outside the sanctuary.
"On the second day, offer a male goat with nothing wrong with it as a sin offering. The altar is to be purified just as it was purified with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, offer a young bull and a ram from the flock, both with nothing wrong with them.
Bring them before the LORD. The priests are to sprinkle salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
"Every day for seven days you are to provide a goat as a sin offering. Also provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both with nothing wrong with them.
For seven days they are to make the altar right and purify it. This is how they will dedicate it.
When these days are over, from the eighth day on, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, says the Lord GOD."
